listener_background: Russian and English native-level; references Hebrew and Mandarin phonetic analogies
raw_observation:
I can clearly hear:
Ki nala atum.
But it feels like the first "k" sound resembles Hebrew "ק" rather than rough English "k" or Rrussian "к" letters. And in addition it have a softening effect of Russian letter "ь" which is used for those purposes. Also it feels a bit "swallowed"-ish effect before the "k" is pronounced...
Regarding the "a" and "u" in "atum I have another interesting observation. 
- the "a" sounds as if it would be Hebrew "ע" as if it would be ancient תנחית Hebrew rather than modern. And in the same time it feels like Chinese 3rd tone. At least slight similarity is definitely there. I wouldn't be able to notice that if not for the "a" sound in "nala" which are both very plain straightforward "a" sound like in Russian "а"
- the "u" is not a flat "у" from Russian. It has a slight of "ю" in it. But a really slight - like to the end of the vowel.
hearing_origin: Contributor reports independent listening, without checking secondary transcript first; prior availability of fan wording in project discussions may have influenced expectations.

phonetic_impressions.observation: Hebrew ק-like, with a palatal-softening impression comparable to Russian ь; a swallowed or constricted quality before onset.
plain a comparable to Russian а
resembles older Hebrew ע-related articulation with a pitch contour reminiscent of Mandarin third tone
slight transition toward Russian ю near end of vowel
